true_positives.matched_candidate:
Crash when Meet location has no destination calendar

`mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array, but the code dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`. Any Google Meet event whose organizer has no destination calendar will throw before the Cal Video fallback can run. The previous code used optional chaining, so this is a regression; guard with `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` or equivalent.
true_positives.reasoning: Both flag the same root cause: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is destructured from `evt.destinationCalendar` and is undefined when that value is null or an empty array, which leads to a null dereference. The candidate seems to point at the Meet/Cal Video fallback code rather than GoogleCalendarService.createEvent/updateEvent, so the location may differ, but the underlying bug is the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google updateEvent loses destination-calendar fallback

When `externalCalendarId` is not supplied, the `find` callback compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, which is `undefined` and therefore never matches a real destination calendar. The previous fallback used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Updates for booking references that lack an external calendar id now send `calendarId: undefined` and fail instead of updating the selected destination calendar.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point at the same find callback comparing cal.externalId to externalCalendarId, which is faulty logic. The golden frames it around the case where externalCalendarId is provided; the candidate frames it around the case where it is undefined. Either way, the underlying bug is the same self-referential comparison, which fails to find the right destination calendar.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Organization slug condition appears inverted

This unrelated change reverses the existing condition: previously `slug` was included only when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` was false, now it is included only when it is true. For self-hosted/no-billing installs, organizations will be created without a slug; for billing-enabled installs, they now get both a direct `slug` and `requestedSlug`, potentially assigning an unverified subdomain before the billing flow. Revert this or document why the condition should flip.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug. The slug condition was flipped so it is now set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true instead of false. As a result, billing-enabled installs get both slug and requestedSlug, while non-billing installs get neither.

false_positives.candidate:
Video references lose credentialId

`referencesToCreate` now sets `credentialId` only for calendar results (`isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`). Non-calendar results are video meetings, and their `result.credentialId` is what lets later cancellation/update code find the video credential. With this change new video references have no `credentialId`, so deletion paths such as `handleCancelBooking` skip `deleteMeeting` and leave orphaned video meetings.

Location updates create references without externalCalendarId or credentialId

`updateLocation` now builds `referencesToCreate` using `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` never returns either field. As a result, after editing a location the newly created booking references omit `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId`, breaking future calendar updates/deletes and forcing legacy fallback behavior. The reference data must be taken from the update result/credential or from the event destination calendar.

Collective team destination calendars dropped when organizer has none

`evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. In that case `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op, so destination calendars collected from the other collective hosts are discarded. This means an organizer without a connected calendar prevents other hosts from receiving calendar invites, which is one of the cases this PR is meant to fix. Initialize the array and push unconditionally when team destinations exist.

Office365 creates all events in the first host's destination calendar

`createEvent` always uses the first element of `event.destinationCalendar` as the target calendar. `EventManager` now invokes `createEvent` once per destination with that host's credential, so the second Office365 host's credential is used against the first host's `externalId`. That creates the event in the wrong calendar or gets a Graph 404, and the second host is not properly invited. The target destination must be matched to the credential being used (or passed explicitly).

Lark creates all events in the first host's destination calendar

`createEvent` takes the first destination calendar from the array and ignores which credential called it. With multiple collective hosts, the second host's Lark credential will try to create the event in the first host's calendar id, so the event either fails or lands in the wrong calendar and the second host does not receive the expected invite. The service needs to select the destination corresponding to the credential used.

CalDAV/BaseCalendar silently skips additional hosts

`createEvent` filters available calendars down to the first destination calendar's `externalId`. When EventManager calls this service for the second host's destination, that externalId belongs to the first host's calendar and does not match any calendar for the second credential, so the filter returns an empty list and no event is created. Because empty responses are treated as success, the missing host event is silent. The filter should target the destination for the current credential rather than always the first array element.

Recurring collective cancellations delete only one calendar reference

The recurring cancellation branch still uses `updatedBooking.references.find(...)` and deletes only the first `_calendar` reference for each booking. With multi-host bookings there are now multiple calendar references, so only one host's recurring events are cancelled while the others remain on calendars. It also runs this work once per outer calendar reference, duplicating calls. It should iterate all calendar references for each updated booking.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reschedule calendar/video deletion races because async forEach is unawaited

`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` is not awaited. The newly added `await getCalendar(...)` yields before `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` is even called, so `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` and the function return happen while the original calendar/video event may still be present. Any rejection from `getCalendar` or the delete calls is also an unhandled rejection instead of being caught by the surrounding `try/catch`. Use `for...of` or `await Promise.all(...)`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same problem: async forEach callbacks for calendar/video deletion are not awaited. This causes races and unhandled rejections that the surrounding try/catch cannot catch. Both recommend for...of or Promise.all as the fix.

false_positives.candidate:
Recurring cancellation API deletes are pushed after Promise.all

In the recurring-booking branch, calendar cancellations are performed inside `forEach(async (credential) => { ... })` without awaiting the callback. After adding `await getCalendar(credential)`, the callback yields before pushing into `apiDeletes`; the later `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` therefore sees an empty `apiDeletes` and returns without waiting for those calendar deletions. Recurring calendar events may never be cancelled before the handler finishes. Collect promises with `await Promise.all(...)` or use a `for...of` loop.

Reschedule cleanup starts after the response because async forEach is unawaited

The callback passed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` is now `async` and contains `await getCalendar(...)`, but `forEach` does not wait for it. Calendar/video cancellation can therefore start after `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` has run and after the function has returned; failures are unhandled. This is the same unsafe pattern as in the Vital reschedule flow and should be converted to `for...of`/`Promise.all`.

Dynamic imports are eagerly started for every app

Each `import("./...")` in the object literal is evaluated as soon as this module is loaded, so all app modules start loading immediately. This does not provide lazy loading and may keep the same startup cost as the previous static imports. If the intent is to load app modules only when used, store loader functions such as `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")` and call the loader at the use site.

getCalendarCredentials now returns promises in its calendar field

`getCalendarCredentials` remains synchronous, but `getCalendar` is now async. As a result the exported helper returns objects whose `calendar` property is `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`. `getConnectedCalendars` in this file awaits it, but any other exported consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` that treats `calendar` as a Calendar will break at runtime or type-check time. Either make `getCalendarCredentials` async and resolve all calendars, or update the type/contract and every caller.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
